rows.verified: Major MEWP hazards include entrapment, overturning, falling from the platform and collision.
The correct MEWP must be selected for the job and site, and its use must be properly planned and managed.
A practised rescue plan is required, and someone on the ground should know how to use the ground controls.
MEWPs should operate on firm, level ground, with temporary covers capable of carrying the applied pressure.
Outriggers must be extended and chocked before raising the platform, using spreader plates where necessary.
Platforms must have effective guardrails and toe boards; suitable work-restraint equipment is required where residual fall risk remains.
Maximum safe wind speed should be defined, and platforms should be inspected after severe weather.
Operators need recognised training plus familiarisation with the specific make and model, and the MEWP must be thoroughly examined at least every six months.
MEWP controls depend on machine type, ground, load, reach, overhead hazards, wind, traffic, rescue arrangements, operator competence and examination status.
MEWP evidence is equipment-, task-, site- and weather-specific and is not an exact parcel-level overturn or fall probability.
Waste and recycling health hazards can enter through skin contact, sharps injection, ingestion or inhalation.
Risk controls should address infectious materials, discarded needles, personal hygiene and suitable welfare facilities.
Common safety hazards include slips and trips, machinery, transport movements and lifting operations.
Sites should use safe operating procedures, competence training and adequate supervision, information and instruction for visitors.
Public access at civic amenity and recycling sites must be considered when managing workplace hazards.
Waste producers must classify waste correctly, with early characterisation where hazardous properties may be present.
Plant operators and other workers must receive suitable training, including first-aid arrangements where required.
Controls should prevent unauthorised entry into large bins and manage the safe stacking of baled waste.
Waste controls depend on waste stream, contamination, sharps, plant, vehicles, public access, processing method, hygiene facilities and worker competence.
Waste and recycling evidence is material-, facility- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury or infection probability.
